1.d4 d5 2.c4 c6 3.cxd5 cxd5 4.Nc3 Nf6 5..strategy: Solid development: the knight guards d4 and heads for a quiet, symmetrical position in which every piece stands well. White keeps the extra move but the symmetry offers little more than a safe game; Black has nothing to fear but also little to attack.

Prepares e2-e4 to build a broad pawn centre and break the symmetry. The cost is development: the pawn takes f3 from the king's knight and opens the e1-h4 diagonal, so Black can strike at the centre first.
1.d4 d5 2.c4 c6 3.cxd5 cxd5 4.Nc3 Nf6 5..name: Slav Defence: Exchange Variation, Boor Attack

1.d4 d5 2.c4 c6 3.cxd5 cxd5 4.Nc3 Nf6 5..strategy: Mirrors White's development and puts the knight where it attacks d4 and covers e5. Black keeps the symmetrical structure and has no weaknesses, so the game stays level and quiet unless White finds a way to use the extra move.
